biography.plain_text: Arthur Wirtz was an American entrepreneur who built his fortune in Chicago real estate before expanding into liquor distribution, banking and professional sport. A University of Michigan graduate and policeman's son, he founded privately held Wirtz Corporation and became an owner of the Chicago Blackhawks and the Chicago Bulls basketball team.

A University of Michigan graduate and policeman's son, he founded privately held Wirtz Corporation and became an owner of the Chicago Blackhawks and the Chicago Bulls basketball team.

confidence.reason: Primary company and club records corroborate contemporary biographical reporting; specific touring practices are independently sourced.

long_biography.plain_text:
Businessman Arthur Wirtz helped turn champion skater Sonja Henie into the centrepiece of a touring entertainment business. Their Hollywood Ice Revue filled major arenas, while a separate production ran at Rockefeller Center. Wirtz organised bookings and travel, including a dedicated train, and helped Henie invest her earnings in property and other businesses.

His work in Chicago extended to the infrastructure serving visitors and conventions. He chaired the city's Urban Transportation District under four mayors and was a founding member of the McCormick Place board. At the Bismarck Hotel, he converted the Palace Theater into a convention room.
